narrative.intro: New Hampshire received $1.7B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. The state logged 3,809 awards with an average award size of $438K. Spending fell year over year, down 42.7% compared with the prior fiscal year to date. Obligations have varied across recent fiscal years: FY21 was $1.8B, FY22 was $1.7B, FY23 was $1.9B, FY24 was $2.9B, and FY25 was $2.9B. The Department of Defense is the dominant buyer, obligating $1.4B so far in FY2026. Other significant buyers include the Department of Transportation with $54M and the Department of Justice with $34.2M. The largest vendors by obligations include BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC. with $760M and SIG SAUER INC. with $297M. Major industry concentrations are in aircraft and defense-related manufacturing, led by Other Aircraft Parts and Auxiliary Equipment Manufacturing at $344M and Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing at $288M. Current-year totals are partial because the fiscal year is still in progress.

sections.heading: How did federal contracting in New Hampshire change year over year?
sections.body: New Hampshire obligations fell 42.7% year over year. State obligations in FY26 to date are $1.7B, after FY25 obligations of $2.9B and FY24 obligations of $2.9B. The recent multi-year sequence shows fluctuations: FY21 was $1.8B, FY22 was $1.7B, and FY23 was $1.9B. Current-year totals are partial because the fiscal year is still in progress.

sections.heading: Which agencies, vendors, and industries lead federal contracting in New Hampshire?
sections.body: The Department of Defense obligated $1.4B and is the largest buying agency in FY2026 to date. BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC. received $760M and SIG SAUER INC. received $297M, making them the top two vendors. Other Aircraft Parts and Auxiliary Equipment Manufacturing is the largest industry by obligations at $344M, followed by Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing at $288M. Additional notable agencies include the Department of Transportation with $54M and the Department of Justice with $34.2M.

faq.q: How much federal contract money goes to New Hampshire?
faq.a: New Hampshire received $1.7B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. The state recorded 3,809 awards with an average award size of $438K. Obligations have shifted over recent years: FY21 was $1.8B, FY22 was $1.7B, FY23 was $1.9B, FY24 was $2.9B, and FY25 was $2.9B. Current-year totals are partial because the fiscal year is still in progress.

faq.q: Which agencies award the most contracts in New Hampshire?
faq.a: The Department of Defense obligated $1.4B and is the largest contracting agency in New Hampshire for FY2026 to date. Other leading buyers include the Department of Transportation with $54M and the Department of Justice with $34.2M. Additional agencies buying in the state include the Department of Veterans Affairs with $29.3M and the Department of Health and Human Services with $20.5M.

faq.q: Who are the largest federal contractors in New Hampshire?
faq.a: BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC. is the largest federal contractor in New Hampshire with $760M in obligations, followed by SIG SAUER INC. with $297M. Other top vendors include ENVISION TECHNOLOGY, LLC with $68.9M and BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION & ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC with $50.2M. Industry concentration is strongest in aircraft and defense-related manufacturing, led by Other Aircraft Parts and Auxiliary Equipment Manufacturing at $344M and Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing at $288M.
